brief.topic: Five checks before you switch to a new model version
brief.audience: PMs and engineers running LLM features in production

coreInsight: A newer model that scores higher on public benchmarks can still be worse on your tasks, so run your own eval set, check format, cost, latency and refusals, and keep a way back.

hooks.text: New model? Don’t just swap it in.
hooks.notes: Fits every model release; the reel gives the checks.
Good line; used as the rule instead.

hooks.text: The upgrade that made your product worse.
hooks.notes: Teases a story the reel doesn’t tell.

caption.opening: A new model version scores higher on public benchmarks. That doesn’t mean it’s better at what your product does.
body:
Before you switch:
→ Run your eval set, old vs new, side by side
→ Check the output format still parses
→ Compare cost and latency per task, not per token
→ Watch for new refusals and changes in answer length
→ Keep the old version available for rollback
Then roll it out like any release: a small share of traffic first.

claims.text: Before switching to a new model version, teams should compare it with the current one on their own eval set and check format adherence, cost, latency, refusals and answer length, and keep a rollback path.
